rationale: C16 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both orders establish a one-time personnel benefit for employees serving in competitive positions on the order date, condition that benefit on a specified period of continuous service, timely agency recommendation, and a Civil Service Commission-prescribed examination, then address military service, excluded employee classes, and Commission regulations. The child adapts C16's acquisition of competitive status into conversion to career or career-conditional appointments and adds later career-system and postal-service details. C11 is also materially relevant because it supplies the career/career-conditional conversion framework, including treatment of indefinite appointees, military absences, and postal employees. C03 closely reinforces C16's template through its amended continuous-service, postal-substitute, agency-recommendation, and military-service provisions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: any employee ... serving in a position in the competitive service under an indefinite appointment or a temporary appointment without a definite time limitation may have his appointment converted to a career or career-conditional appointment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any employee of the Federal Government without competitive status who on the date of this order is serving in an active-duty status in an office or position in the competitive service ... shall acquire a competitive status upon compliance with the following conditions
shared_material.explanation: Both open with the same basic one-time mechanism: employees occupying competitive-service positions on the order date receive a new civil-service status or appointment after satisfying enumerated conditions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall have completed two years of continuous service immediately preceding the date of this order ... shall be recommended ... by his agency within one year ... [and] shall have passed a qualifying examination ... or shall meet such noncompetitive examination standards as the Civil Service Commission shall prescribe
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall have served continuously ... during the two years immediately prior to the date of this order ... must be recommended by the head of the agency ... within six months ... [and] must successfully qualify in such suitable noncompetitive examination as the Civil Service Commission may prescribe
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive sequence of a two-year service threshold, timely agency recommendation, and Commission-controlled examination is substantially replicated with adjusted details.

shared_material.child_excerpt: service shall include military service if the employee shall have left a competitive position to enter the armed forces ... and shall have been re-employed ... within 120 days after discharge under honorable conditions
shared_material.parent_excerpt: military service shall not be regarded as a break in service
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly preserve eligibility despite intervening military service, with the child elaborating the machinery and reemployment deadline.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall not apply to postmasters or rural carriers ... The Civil Service Commission may prescribe such regulations as may be necessary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall not be applicable to (a) postmasters; (b) rural carriers ... The Civil Service Commission shall promulgate regulations to effectuate the purposes of this order
shared_material.explanation: The child repeats both specific excluded postal classes and the closing delegation of implementing authority to the Commission.
